correctness.rationale: For assigned matching signs, the exact fiber equation is w_next=a*s*w and tangent determinant is -2b*s. A trajectory approaching a compact K in the invariant diagonal satisfies w_n->0. Infinitely many opposite-sign visits imply |u_n|<=|w_n|->0 and, since w_next=+/- (a*u_n-y_n), y_n->0, forcing the origin into K, contradiction. Eventually the signs agree and |w| multiplies by |a|>=1, hence w vanishes exactly at a finite iterate. The original four open-branch affine determinants are -2ab!=0, so every inverse image of a null set is null up to zero-volume switching planes. The union of finite diagonal preimages is null. When 0<|a|<1 and 0<b<(1-|a|)/2, the exhibited positive diagonal fixed point has tangent eigenvalue absolute values bounded by (|a|+sqrt(a^2+8b))/2<1 and normal multiplier a, giving an open ambient basin. The normal-exponent and finite-time laws follow exactly from block diagonal derivatives and scalar fiber updates; the 4050 finite symbolic checks supplement rather than establish the infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A fixed-point eigenvalue or a positive normal exponent alone does not imply the global basin theorem: opposite sign branches could in principle cause finite transverse resets. The proof shows that infinitely many opposite sign visits while approaching K force a subsequence to the origin, excluded by hypothesis, then forces eventual exact diagonal entrance. Every inverse branch is affine and invertible, hence the finite-entrance set is null. The neutral |a|=1 case lies outside ordinary strict normal repulsion arguments, and below the barrier an actual open-basin sink exists.

originality.rationale: The generating map, its diagonal reduction and its smooth-branch Jacobian, including specific fixed-point normal eigenvalues, are already published. The asserted contribution is the global zero-Lebesgue-volume basin barrier for every nonempty compact invariant diagonal set avoiding the origin at |a|>=1, including the neutral case and intersections with switching lines at nonzero y. Proof needs a nonlinear opposite-sign exclusion and preimage-nullity argument, not just the previously known fixed-point eigenvalue. The existential positive-basin sharpness construction supports the structural boundary. Earlier transverse instability results concern different systems; priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The original Lozi study identifies coexisting geometrically thin thread and sheet-like invariant behavior. A physical attractor must attract positive full-dimensional volume, whereas a set restricted to an invariant plane need not. The theorem gives a sharp and uniform full-space obstruction for any nonempty compact diagonal invariant set avoiding one singular point, even at zero transverse exponent and despite switching-line intersections. An explicit sink family below the threshold shows the boundary is substantive. The result addresses a central structural question of the motivating model, not a finite table or a rephrased known fixed-point calculation.
